vocab.context: The word Genos said watching Saitama punch a meteor apart. The reaction that fills anime's most breathtaking moments — power, beauty, surprise — all one word.
The sound of something clicking. A strategist like Shikamaru or Lelouch says this right before explaining why they were ten steps ahead.
The sound of a decision being made. A fist clenched, a deep breath taken. 'Yoshi!' signals the hero is ready to face whatever comes next.
Pure triumph in two syllables. Shouted after landing a finishing blow, passing a test, or any hard-won victory. The past tense of 'yaru' (to do).
Technically means 'lie/falsehood' but used constantly as a shocked reaction. 'USO DA!' is iconic from Clannad — a cry of disbelief and denial.
'Chotto matte kudasai!' in polite form. The frantic chase scene staple — the protagonist running after someone who doesn't know the truth yet.
The word Rock Lee says to Gai-sensei when told he can fight again. The word Violet Evergarden finally learns to write for others. When characters who rarely speak say this, the audience cries.
Casual apology. 'Gomen ne' is softer. 'Gomen nasai' is the formal version. In anime, often said with tears — the most emotional syllables in the language.

meanings.en: it's okay / I'm fine / are you alright?
meanings.pt-BR: tudo bem / estou bem / você está bem?

vocab.context: Works as both a question and an answer. The wounded hero says 'daijoubu' through gritted teeth. The worried friend asks 'daijoubu?' with wide eyes.

meanings.en: you can do it! / hang in there! / do your best!
meanings.pt-BR: vai com tudo! / você consegue! / não desiste!

vocab.context: Screamed from the stands at the exact moment Deku's legs give out but he keeps moving. Imperative — 'you must not stop now.' The crowd's roar made into a single word.

meanings.en: good luck / do your best (to someone leaving)

vocab.context: The quiet send-off. Said by Hinata to Naruto before the chunin exam. Not a command — a prayer. 'I'll be thinking of you.' Said to someone leaving, not mid-battle.
The mission accepted. Past tense of 'wakaru' (to understand). Said before the hero runs off to do exactly what they just agreed to — or the opposite.

meanings.pt-BR: sério? / de verdade? / tá me zuando?

vocab.context: The disbelieving double-take. Slightly informal — used more in modern slice-of-life than shonen. 'Maji de?!' with rising intonation = total shock.
Originally meant dangerous/bad, now also means 'amazingly good'. The same word covers a disaster and a stunning sunset. Context is everything.
Casual affirmation between friends. Softer than 'hai'. A quiet 'un' with a nod is one of the most intimate exchanges in slice-of-life anime.
The sharp intake of breath turned into a word. Often followed by silence — the pause before the revelation hits. You'll hear it at every plot twist.

meanings.en: leave it to me! / count on me!

vocab.context: The hero stepping forward. 'Ore ni makasero!' — Leave it to me! Said before the climactic fight or the moment of self-sacrifice. Maximum confidence.

meanings.en: let's go! / here we go! / move out!

vocab.context: 'Iku' (go) + 'zo' (assertive masculine particle). The rallying cry before every charge. Goku says it. Naruto says it. Your squad needs to hear it.
Said at the door, every time, without fail. The response is 'okaeri'. In anime, a character who comes home to silence — no okaeri — has already lost everything.
Every school anime begins with this. The formal version is 'ohayou gozaimasu' — you know which version classmates use and which homeroom teachers expect.
Said at lights-out in dorm arcs, after emotional conversations through a bedroom door, and in the quiet moment before a battle the next day. More weight than it looks.

meanings.en: let's eat / I humbly receive (said before meals)
meanings.pt-BR: bom apetite / vou receber (dito antes das refeições)
meanings.es: buen provecho / lo recibo con gratitud (antes de comer)

vocab.context: Hands together, eyes closed, a beat before the first bite. Every school lunch scene, every family dinner, every convenience store bench meal in an isekai. You cannot watch anime without hearing this daily.

meanings.en: I'm off / I'll be back (said when leaving home)
meanings.pt-BR: estou indo / até logo (ao sair de casa)
meanings.es: me voy / ahora vuelvo (al salir de casa)

vocab.context: Said at the door when leaving home. The expected response is 'itterasshai'. The hero says this before the decisive battle. The student before the entrance exam. Small words, enormous weight.

meanings.en: take care / see you later (to someone leaving)
meanings.pt-BR: vai com cuidado / até logo (para quem está saindo)
meanings.es: cuídate / hasta luego (a quien se va)

vocab.context: The response to ittekimasu — said by whoever stays behind. In anime, a character who leaves to silence — no itterasshai — has stepped into the unknown alone. The silence is the point.
